q-103212.name: Question 1
q-103212.worked_solution:
To compute ${a}_{4},$ we first need to compute ${a}_{3}.$ So, we substitute $n=1$ into the recursive formula, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{n+2} & ={a}_{n+1}+{a}_{n} \\ {a}_{1+2} & ={a}_{1+1}+{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{3} & ={a}_{2}+{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{3} & =1+(-1) \\ {a}_{3} & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Next, to compute ${a}_{4},$ we substitute $n=2$ into the recursive formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2+2} & ={a}_{2+1}+{a}_{2} \\ {a}_{4} & ={a}_{3}+{a}_{2} \\ {a}_{4} & =0+1 \\ {a}_{4} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, ${a}_{4}=1.$

q-103212.html:
Question 1
?

If an+2=an+1+an with a1=−1 and a2=1, then a4=

a
1
b
2
c
−1
d
0
e
3
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

To compute a4, we first need to compute a3. So, we substitute n=1 into the recursive formula, as follows:

an+2=an+1+ana1+2=a1+1+a1a3=a2+a1a3=1+(−1)a3=0

Next, to compute a4, we substitute n=2 into the recursive formula: a2+2=a2+1+a2a4=a3+a2a4=0+1a4=1

Therefore, a4=1.

q-103220.name: Question 2
q-103220.problem:
The recursive formula for the Fibonacci numbers is 

$$
{a}_{n+2}={a}_{n+1}+{a}_{n},\,{a}_{1}={a}_{2}=1,\,n\ge 1.
$$

What is the eighth number in the sequence?
q-103220.worked_solution:
Substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{1+2} & ={a}_{1+1}+{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{3} & ={a}_{2}+{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{3} & =1+1 \\ {a}_{3} & =2\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{2+2} & ={a}_{2+1}+{a}_{2} \\ {a}_{4} & ={a}_{3}+{a}_{2} \\ {a}_{4} & =2+1 \\ {a}_{4} & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=3$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{3+2} & ={a}_{3+1}+{a}_{3} \\ {a}_{5} & ={a}_{4}+{a}_{3} \\ {a}_{5} & =3+2 \\ {a}_{5} & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=4$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{4+2} & ={a}_{4+1}+{a}_{4} \\ {a}_{6} & ={a}_{5}+{a}_{4} \\ {a}_{6} & =5+3 \\ {a}_{6} & =8\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=5$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{5+2} & ={a}_{5+1}+{a}_{5} \\ {a}_{7} & ={a}_{6}+{a}_{5} \\ {a}_{7} & =8+5 \\ {a}_{7} & =13\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=6$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{6+2} & ={a}_{6+1}+{a}_{6} \\ {a}_{8} & ={a}_{7}+{a}_{6} \\ {a}_{8} & =13+8 \\ {a}_{8} & =21\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $21$ is the eighth number in the sequence.

q-103220.html:
Question 2
?

The recursive formula for the Fibonacci numbers is an+2=an+1+an,a1=a2=1,n≥1.

What is the eighth number in the sequence?

a
34
b
8
c
21
d
13
e
55
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Substituting n=1 into the recursive formula gives: a1+2=a1+1+a1a3=a2+a1a3=1+1a3=2

Substituting n=2 into the recursive formula gives: a2+2=a2+1+a2a4=a3+a2a4=2+1a4=3

Substituting n=3 into the recursive formula gives: a3+2=a3+1+a3a5=a4+a3a5=3+2a5=5

Substituting n=4 into the recursive formula gives:

a4+2=a4+1+a4a6=a5+a4a6=5+3a6=8

Substituting n=5 into the recursive formula gives: a5+2=a5+1+a5a7=a6+a5a7=8+5a7=13

Substituting n=6 into the recursive formula gives:

a6+2=a6+1+a6a8=a7+a6a8=13+8a8=21

Therefore, 21 is the eighth number in the sequence.

q-214157.name: Question 3
q-214157.worked_solution:
The recursion relation is

$$
f(n+2)=f(n+1)+f(n).
$$

Substituting $n=1$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(1+2) & =f(1+1)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =f(2)+f(1) \\ f(3) & =(-2)+7 \\ f(3) & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $n=2$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(2+2) & =f(2+1)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =f(3)+f(2) \\ f(4) & =5+(-2) \\ f(4) & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Similarly, substituting $n=3,4,5,6$ into the recursive formula gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(5) & =f(3+2)=f(3+1)+f(3)=f(4)+f(3)=3+5=8, \\ f(6) & =f(4+2)=f(4+1)+f(4)=f(5)+f(4)=8+3=11, \\ f(7) & =f(5+2)=f(5+1)+f(5)=f(6)+f(5)=11+8=19, \\ f(8) & =f(6+2)=f(6+1)+f(6)=f(7)+f(6)=19+11=30.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $f(8)=30.$
